subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Should OpenClaw pursue #35203 as phased core primitives, route the full collaboration stack to plugins/ClawHub with only missing SDK seams in core, or decline the umbrella stack and track only narrower items?
rationale: The request crosses persistent state, memory visibility, agent delegation, config, cost governance, and security boundaries, so code automation cannot choose the permanent product boundary safely.

options.title: Phase Core Seams First
options.body: Keep the umbrella RFC open, require a short maintainer design for storage/security/API boundaries, and accept only narrow PRs that fit the chosen phases.

options.title: Route Full Stack To Plugins
options.body: Treat capability profiling, blackboard, and orchestration as plugin/ClawHub work while opening focused core issues only for missing plugin APIs.

options.title: Decline Umbrella Stack
options.body: Close this RFC as too broad for core and keep narrower items such as #42475, #60572, #65403, and #66010 as the only canonical work.

recommendation.title: Phase Core Seams First
recommendation.body: Keep the umbrella RFC open, require a short maintainer design for storage/security/API boundaries, and accept only narrow PRs that fit the chosen phases.

likelyOwner.reason: He is tied to the original subagent and usage-cost surfaces and is the clearest owner for VISION/core-boundary product direction.
